overview.en:
This is an online action game built around a generative AI model. Three hunters face one boss player. The hunters choose prompts, and AI generates a monster in real time. The boss player controls that monster, and the hunters have to fight it.

The game combines the randomness of a roguelike with the interaction of a party game. Generative AI makes the monster different each round. Players can pick some really nasty traits, so there’s plenty of room to troll each other.

Right now, the 3v1 PvP is done, the 3-player PvE is done, and the single-player offline boss fight is done. It’s adapted for MacBook, iPad and controllers.
overview.zh:
这是一款结合生成式 AI 模型的联机动作游戏，三名猎人对抗一名 Boss 玩家。猎人各自选择提示词，AI 据此实时生成怪物，再由 Boss 玩家操控这只怪物与他们对抗。

游戏把 Roguelike 的随机性和派对游戏的互动结合在一起。AI 让每局的怪物都不一样，玩家还可以选一些很坑人的词条，在对抗中互坑，让游戏更有意思。

现在 3v1 的 PvP 已经完成，三人 PvE 完成，单人单机 Boss 战完成，适配 MacBook、iPad 和手柄。

caption.en: One hunter against the boss, offline.
caption.zh: 一名猎人对抗 Boss，无需联网。

caption.en: Two players online: first as the boss, then as a hunter.
caption.zh: 两名玩家联机：先操控 Boss，再换成猎人。

paragraphs.en: I bought a lot of ready-made assets online and directed the AI myself. After more than a dozen rounds of fixing and tuning, I finally got a high-precision map.
paragraphs.zh: 我大量购买网上现成的素材，自己指挥 AI，经过十几轮的修改和调优，最后实现了高精度地图。

caption.en: Starwell Oasis, concept for the current map
caption.zh: 星井绿洲，现在这张地图的概念图

caption.en: Early two-player online prototype: hunter versus the boss-controlled monster.
caption.zh: 早期两人联机原型：猎人与 Boss 操控的怪物对抗。

overview.en: The player enters from a recruitment poster and writes to the email on it. A fictional professor assigns Python homework and mentions being out of town. The whole thing is about Camus’s absurdism. When effort no longer brings progress, players start to question the rules themselves and jump out of the box.
overview.zh: 玩家从一张招生海报进入，给海报上的邮箱写信，一位虚构的教授会布置 Python 作业，并说自己正在外地。整个游戏讲的是加缪的荒诞主义：当努力不再换来进展，玩家开始质疑规则本身，跳出框架。

design_question.en: Can a digital system make absurdity something we experience?
design_question.zh: 数字系统能否让人切身体会到荒诞？

paragraphs.en: We shared the poster through public social accounts as if we were promoting a coding boot camp. If you write to the email on the poster, you will receive an automatic reply. The email includes a programming assignment. I wanted all of the flow to look very normal, so that at first glance people cannot see any difference.
paragraphs.zh: 海报通过公共社交账号发布，假装在宣传一个编程训练营。给海报上的邮箱写信会收到一封自动回复，邮件里留了一份编程作业。我想让整个流程看起来都很正常，乍一看看不出任何异样。

caption.zh: Leet Code Academy 招生海报

paragraphs.en: The homework is to fix a weighted average function in Python. The last test uses random inputs but insists the answer is 42, so even a correct function can fail.
paragraphs.zh: 作业是修复一个 Python 加权平均函数。最后一个测试用随机输入，却硬要答案是 42，所以函数写对了也可能过不了。

paragraphs.en: Because players keep getting stuck, they question whether the autograder has a problem. When they see the grading rules, they find the clue was hidden in the rules: the address of the school website. I hope at this step they realize that what they are doing is repetitive and mechanical, and if they think carefully, it is actually meaningless.
paragraphs.zh: 玩家一直卡着，就会质疑自动评分程序是不是有问题。看到打分规则之后，会发现线索就藏在规则里：学校网站的地址。我希望他们在这一步意识到，自己做的事情是重复的、机械的，再仔细想想，其实毫无意义。

paragraphs.en: The website looks like an outdated university portal. A course is missing, and bold letters are scattered across the pages. They are the puzzle.
paragraphs.zh: 网站做成一个过时的大学门户：有一门课缺失，各页散落着粗体字母，这些就是谜题。

paragraphs.en: There are two AI assistants on the website. The first talks with you like an advisor, while hinting at the meaning behind absurdism. It gives hints, but also asks what meaning is. In the end it still gives you the account and password.
paragraphs.zh: 网站上有两个 AI 助手。第一个像顾问一样和你探讨，同时暗示荒诞主义的意义；它会给提示，其实是在反问意义是什么，最后还是会给你账号和密码。

caption.en: Leet Code Academy homepage and helper chatbot
caption.zh: Leet Code Academy 首页与聊天助手

paragraphs.en: After logging in comes a conversation with the John Smith bot, the fictional professor. It does not resolve the puzzles into one answer. It talks with you about absurdism and your experience of the game. I hope players leave with a better understanding of the concept.
paragraphs.zh: 登录后是与 John Smith 机器人的对话，也就是那位虚构的教授。它不会把谜题归结成一个答案，而是作为最后的启发者和总结者，和你聊荒诞主义和这段游戏的体验。我希望玩家离开游戏后，对这个概念有更多理解。

caption.en: An excerpt from the final conversation with John Smith
caption.zh: 与 John Smith 的最终对话节选
Jupyter Notebook 中的编程作业

process_note.en: The missing course is CSE 1A. The bold letters across the site spell “meaning”. Encoding it in Base64 gives the password. The username, “lukewam”, is hidden in the URL.
process_note.zh: 课程目录里找不到 CSE 1A。各页的粗体字母拼出“meaning”，将这个词转为 Base64 编码，便能得到密码。用户名“lukewam”藏在网址中。

subtitle.en: A mobile game prototype for climate action
subtitle.zh: 鼓励气候行动的手机游戏原型

role.zh: 原型与界面开发负责人

overview.en: A digital pet based on Tamagotchi. The idea is to get players to start from small things to protect the environment. Every day you complete tasks by taking photos, and the tasks are small things like taking the bus or picking up trash. You earn coins, and you can use them to buy food, to dress up your polar bear, and to add other players. I was involved from the research at the start to the low-fidelity and hi-fi prototypes.
overview.zh: 这是一个根据 Tamagotchi 改的电子宠物，意在倡导玩家从小事开始保护环境。玩家每天通过拍照完成任务来赚取金币，任务都是很小的事情，比如坐公交、捡垃圾。金币可以用来买食物、装扮北极熊，也可以去社交，加别的玩家。我从开始的调研一直到后面的低保真、高保真原型都有参与。

paragraphs.en: We gave the survey first to people around us, then to strangers on the street, more than 100 people in all. Most were young people, but the ages ranged widely. What we cared about most: many people are willing to do things for the environment and care about it, but they don’t deliberately keep it up. And they find this kind of educational game especially boring.
paragraphs.zh: 问卷先发给周围的人，再发给街上的陌生人，一共 100 多人，大部分是年轻人，年纪从小到大都有。最让我们在意的是，很多人愿意做环保的事，也很在意环保，但并没有很刻意地去坚持。第二是他们觉得这类教育游戏特别无聊。

paragraphs.en: From the three options, a racing game, a recycling RPG, and a pet, we picked the polar bear, because the polar bear represents the glaciers. Glacier melting is the most direct example of the greenhouse effect. We wanted to make it as cute as possible, social, and lightweight, so players can play it every day. It should fit the Gen Z trend, not be a game that is education for the sake of education.
paragraphs.zh: 赛车、回收 RPG 和电子宠物三个方案里选了北极熊，因为北极熊代表冰川，冰川融化是温室效应最直接的例子。我们想把它做得尽量可爱、社交化、轻量化，让玩家每天都能玩，更符合 Z 世代的潮流，而不是一个只为了教育而教育的游戏。

caption.en: Large-scale and small-scale climate action survey results
caption.zh: 不同规模气候行动的问卷结果

paragraphs.en: A and B are two flows with different button patterns, made in Figma for customization, task progress, and task history. In A you have to tap more, and the screens are hidden behind buttons. I designed B to be more intuitive. The calendar and the task records are placed directly on the screen, and the task preview has a summary. My idea was to give information to the user more directly.
paragraphs.zh: A 和 B 两套流程在 Figma 里做，包括装扮、任务进度和任务记录，按键模式不一样。A 的模式里需要点的操作更多，界面都被藏在按键里面了。我设计的 B 更直观：日历和任务记录直接放在页面上，任务预览里有任务概述。我的想法就是，首先要把信息更直观地给用户。

paragraphs.en: We first tested the flows within the team, then with people around us, and recorded how long the tasks took, self-ratings, and comments. B was chosen.
paragraphs.zh: 测试是我们先在小组内部完成内部评价，然后再把它分发给周围的人评价，记录了完成时间、自评和评论，最后选了 B。

caption.en: Task history and calendar low-fidelity wireframes
caption.zh: 任务记录与日历线框图

paragraphs.en: The home screen has the bear, the tasks, progress, and streaks. I designed the feeding and dress-up systems, including the inventory, the icons, the items, and the tasks. You earn coins by completing tasks, like taking the bus every day or using a reusable bag, and you confirm a task by taking a photo. In the food shop you buy food for the bear, and in the shop you buy decorations. There is also a profile page.
paragraphs.zh: 首页有北极熊、任务、进度和连续打卡。我设计了喂养和装扮系统，包括物品栏、图标、道具和任务。金币通过完成任务来赚。任务比如说每天坐公交，或者用可重复使用的购物袋，然后通过拍照来确认完成任务。食物商店给北极熊买食物，商店买装饰，还有个人资料页。

paragraphs.en: The friends page is the social part. Others can see your polar bear, and you can show off your bear and your decorations.
paragraphs.zh: 好友页是社交的一部分，让别人看到、也向别人展示自己的北极熊和装饰。

paragraphs.en: What I liked most was turning the concept into something real, and making a topic as educational as the environment into a game I would actually want to play.
paragraphs.zh: 做完之后我觉得最有意思的是把概念落实到行动中，把环保这么教育性的概念做进一个我真的愿意玩的游戏里。

caption.zh: 首页：北极熊、打卡记录与任务进度

role.zh: 交互设计与测试负责人

overview.en: A VR game for Meta Quest 2, made in Unity and C#. Somewhere in the ruins of a city there is an injured person. The player has to walk through the ruins, find them, and choose the first-aid items they need. Each item is used in its own way. There is also a time limit: if it runs out, the injured person dies. I was responsible for user interaction and testing, from the controllers to hand tracking.
overview.zh: 这是一个用 Unity 和 C# 做的 Meta Quest 2 VR 游戏。城市废墟里有一名伤者，玩家需要穿过废墟找到他，选择需要的急救物品，每种物品的使用方式都不同。游戏还有时间限制，超时伤者就会死亡。我负责用户交互和测试，从手柄到手部追踪。

paragraphs.en: The medical room prototype in Unity was for testing user interaction. The controller selects things with a ray, and different buttons switch between teleporting and picking up. The arrows for finding the injured came after the medical room. The menu holds the equipment and also text input. You can search for the equipment you need, read the injured person’s information, and give a diagnosis.
paragraphs.zh: 最开始在 Unity 里搭的医疗室原型，是用来做用户交互测试的。手柄用射线选东西，按不同的键可以传送或者拿起。用箭头引导找伤者是医疗室之后的事。菜单里除了器材，还有需要输入的文字。可以通过搜索找到需要的器材，也可以查看伤者的信息，然后给出诊断。

title.en: Keeping the menu with the player

paragraphs.en: In testing, the menu stayed still and did not follow the player. We first attached it to the player, but its height blocked the view, so we adjusted the height step by step and then let it hide while the player moves.
paragraphs.zh: 测试时发现菜单固定不动，不跟随玩家。我们先把它绑到玩家身上，但高度会挡住视野，于是逐步调整高度，再让它在移动时隐藏。

caption.en: Patient and medical equipment input flow
caption.zh: 伤者与医疗器材输入流程

paragraphs.en: After that we added hand tracking with the Meta Interaction SDK. Fingers were hard to detect, so in the end we kept only the thumb pressing against different fingers, a fist, and an open hand. For the virtual keyboard, you first press the fingers together to bring up the menu, then type by touching the keys with a finger.
paragraphs.zh: 之后我们用 Meta Interaction SDK 加入了手部追踪。手指很难被检测到，最后只留下大拇指与不同手指的按压，以及握拳和张手。虚拟键盘是先用手指按压调出菜单，再用手指触碰输入。

caption.en: Hand gestures keyboard and teleport interaction flow
caption.zh: 手势、键盘与传送操作流程
通过手部追踪操作虚拟键盘

design_question.en: How can selecting, moving, and finding help feel clear inside VR?
design_question.zh: 在 VR 中，如何让选取物品、移动和寻找伤者都容易上手？

subtitle.en: A small vehicle learning to read a track

role.en: Hardware design and tracking software development lead
role.zh: 硬件设计与循迹开发负责人

overview.en: We made a small car that can drive by itself. The car can respond to road signs by parking, speeding up, slowing down, or stopping. I was responsible for the hardware and the tracking software.
overview.zh: 这个项目是做一辆能自动驾驶的小车。最后小车可以根据路标自己做出相应动作，比如泊车、加速、减速，以及看到停车标志时停下。硬件和循迹软件由我负责。

paragraphs.en: The car has an acrylic chassis. I designed it in LightBurn and laser cut it. On it there is the NVIDIA chip and a lidar, a camera, and a central VESC motor controller. We 3D printed a protective shell, to protect the NVIDIA chip and to mount the camera. The shell was modeled in Blender. We also designed its wiring and layout.
paragraphs.zh: 车身是亚克力板，我用 LightBurn 设计，再激光切割。上面有 NVIDIA 芯片、一个激光雷达、一个摄像头，以及中央的 VESC 电机控制器。我们 3D 打印了一个保护壳，用来保护 NVIDIA 芯片和安装摄像头，外壳在 Blender 里建模。我们也设计了它的走线与布局。

paragraphs.en: We can control it remotely through a laptop, and receive real-time video. You can operate it with the arrow keys.
paragraphs.zh: 通过笔记本可以远程操纵它，接收实时视频，用方向键就能操作。

caption.en: Front sensor mounting and cable routing
caption.zh: 前置传感器的固定与走线

title.zh: 用 30 圈驾驶训练模型

paragraphs.en: We drove 30 laps with Donkey Car to record training data, then trained the model on a remote server. After training, at the beginning the car did not know how to drive, because the reflection was very serious. The light on the site was very strong.
paragraphs.zh: 我们用 Donkey Car 开了三十圈记录数据，在远程服务器上训练模型。训练完之后，车一开始并不知道怎么跑，因为场地光线特别强，反光特别严重。

paragraphs.en: What we could do was to train repeatedly at different times of the day, and use a large amount of data to resist the reflection, because the lights and the reflections are at different places at different times.
paragraphs.zh: 我们能做的是在一天的不同时段反复训练，用大量数据来抵抗反光的干扰，因为不同时段灯光和反光落的位置也不一样。

caption.en: Onboard training footage from the marked track, with curves and strong window light.
caption.zh: 车载镜头记录了赛道弯道和窗边强光下的训练过程。

caption.en: A second training recording on tiled flooring, using blue tape to mark the route.
caption.zh: 另一段训练录像，路线由瓷砖地面上的蓝色胶带标出。

paragraphs.en: Later we switched to OpenCV to respond to colors, because training this way was slow and not very accurate. With color, black, white, and yellow identify the track better, and light blue marks its boundary. Above a certain horizon line, blue means parking and red means the stop sign. By recognizing the 50 and the 100 on the signs, the car decides whether to speed up or slow down.
paragraphs.zh: 后来改成用 OpenCV 按颜色响应，因为一直这样训练特别慢，准确率也不高。按颜色响应时，黑色、白色和黄色能更好地识别赛道，浅蓝色是赛道的边界。特定地平线以上的蓝色是泊车标志，红色是停车标志。通过辨认路标上的 50 和 100，确认是加速还是减速。

design_question.en: What changes when a driving model meets a reflective, unevenly lit track?
design_question.zh: 赛道反光、光照不均时，驾驶模型会怎样表现？

caption.en: The laser-cut acrylic platform before fitting the electronics
caption.zh: 安装电子部件前的激光切割亚克力平台

subtitle.en: An Android app for planning a zoo visit
subtitle.zh: 规划动物园行程的 Android 应用

overview.en: Zoo Navigator is an Android app about the map of the San Diego Zoo. You can choose which exhibits you want to go and see, and it tells you the closest way to walk. We used real San Diego Zoo data. It can also plan the route for you and give you a best route to follow, if you give it a whole list. I led the backend development and the search algorithm, and I also wrote some of the database search and the navigation.
overview.zh: Zoo Navigator 是一个基于 San Diego Zoo 地图的 Android 应用。你可以选择想去看的园区，它会告诉你怎么走最近。我们用的是真实的 San Diego Zoo 数据。如果输入一整个清单，它也能帮你规划出最佳路线。我负责后端开发和搜索算法，也写了一部分数据库搜索和导航。

title.en: From search to a visit list

paragraphs.en: First is search. The search can use part of an animal’s name, so visitors don’t have to write the full name every time. They can also write a related nickname. After that they put the places they want to go into a list, and based on this list they can also choose a simpler guide or the detailed navigation. What I was responsible for was the search and the navigation system in this flow.
paragraphs.zh: 首先是搜索。搜索可以只输入动物名字的一部分，游客不用每次都写全名，也可以写相关的昵称。之后他们把想去的地方放进清单，再根据清单选择更简洁的导览或者详细的导航。这个流程里的搜索和导航系统由我负责。

title.en: Turning the map into a graph

paragraphs.en: We used the real map of the San Diego Zoo. We first turned the map into nodes by hand, then added weighted paths between the nodes to represent the distances between them. Dijkstra’s algorithm then calculates the shortest path from the visitor’s position to the stops they chose.
paragraphs.zh: 我们用的是 San Diego Zoo 真实的园区地图。先手动把地图做成节点，再在节点之间加入带权重的路径，模拟它们之间的路程。然后用 Dijkstra 算法，算出从游客位置到所选园区最近的路。

title.en: Testing the parts and the journey

paragraphs.en: We built the app in Android Studio, and used different modules to develop the different functions separately. I was also responsible for unit testing, doing unit tests on the different features, and at the end we did the integration test to look at all the functions together, including search, planning, navigation, detailed navigation, and toggling between the different navigation modes.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在 Android Studio 里开发，不同功能放在不同模块里分开开发。我也负责单元测试，对各个功能分别测试，最后再做集成测试，把搜索、规划、导航、详细导航和导航模式切换放在一起检验。

caption.en: Zoo Navigator animal search and visit planner
caption.zh: 动物园导航 动物搜索与行程规划

design_question.en: How can a list of animals become a route a visitor can follow?
design_question.zh: 如何根据想看的动物安排游览路线？

overview.en: Paintings of ordinary life, and the feelings that linger within it. These works move between realism and abstraction, gathering fragments of memory, reflection, and quiet strangeness.
overview.zh: 这些画记录日常生活中久久不散的情绪，在写实与抽象之间，留下记忆、思绪，以及平静生活里不易察觉的异样。

caption.en: Sakya — 20" × 16", oil pastel & acrylic on canvas, 2024
caption.zh: 《释迦》｜20 × 16 英寸，布面油画棒与丙烯，2024

role.zh: 构思、绘画、程序与装置制作

overview.en:
This work is an installation that combines projection and oil painting. On the wall are four self-portraits, all of the same subject, which is my face. The camera points at the most abstract one, the one made of lines. YOLO and CLIP detect what the camera can see, but they cannot detect that the painting is a face, my face.

The audience, with the context given by the other three paintings and their own past experience, can see that it is a face.
overview.zh:
这个作品是一个结合投影和油画的装置。墙上是我的四张自画像，画的都是同一个主题，就是我的脸。摄像头对着的是其中最抽象、用线条表示的那一张，YOLO 和 CLIP 检测摄像头看到的东西，但它们检测不出画上是一张脸，是我的脸。

观众结合另外三张画给的语境，加上自己过往的经历，却能看出那是一张脸。

label.zh: 阅读论文《AI 结构主义》· PDF，13 页

paragraphs.en: The machine itself does not have the social structure or the shared memory that humans have. There are three ways of seeing it: first, you only see its shape; second, through your past social experience and memory you judge that this is a person; third, if you are my close friend, you know this person is me.
paragraphs.zh: 机器本身是没有记忆的，没有社会结构，也没有像人类一样的共同记忆。三种看的区别：第一，你只看到形状；第二，你通过过去的社会经验和记忆，判断出这是一个人；第三，如果你是我的好朋友，你会知道这个人是我。

paragraphs.en: Machinery structuralism gives structuralism a more contemporary definition: the meaning that exists between humans, AI, and machines, and the relations between us and images, and between computers and images.
paragraphs.zh: 机械结构主义想给结构主义一个更当代的定义：人、AI 和机械之间彼此存在的意义，以及我们与图像、电脑与图像之间的关系。

caption.en: Portrait recognition study. CLIP scores show relative matches within the chosen label set.
caption.zh: 绘画识别实验。CLIP 分数表示图像与所选标签的相对匹配程度。

caption.en: A few painted marks are also read as a face. Scores are relative to the selected labels.
caption.zh: 几笔五官色块，也被识别为一张脸。分数仅表示与所选标签的相对匹配程度。

paragraphs.en: The film generates an image from a sentence describing a face. The eighteen small squares in Aperture correspond to the generation process of each word. I want to use it to show how machines understand vision, and the difference from how humans understand images.
paragraphs.zh: 影片是用一句描述面孔的话生成图像，Aperture 里的十八个小格分别对应每个词的生成过程。我希望用它展示机器对视觉的理解，以及和人类理解图片的区别。

caption.en: Attention maps across generation steps. Edited as a forward-and-reverse loop.
caption.zh: 逐词注意力图；正放与倒放组成循环。

paragraphs.en: The projection is a realistic face dissolving into abstraction, so a concrete face appears in the abstract painting, simulating how generative AI turns the latent space of a diffusion model into an image. The other projection shows the confidence score.
paragraphs.zh: 投影是一张写实的脸溶解成抽象，于是抽象画中浮现出一个具象的人脸，模拟生成式 AI 在扩散模型里从潜空间变成图片的样子。另一个投影展示置信度分数。

paragraphs.en: The latent space is the shared memory of the machines: they understand the face in the noise, but not the face in the abstract lines. Jim Campbell’s work made me notice that light is also a part of the image.
paragraphs.zh: 潜空间是机器自己的共同记忆：它们能理解噪点中的人脸，却理解不了抽象线条里的人脸。Jim Campbell 的作品让我留意，光如何影响我们辨认一幅图像。

paragraphs.en: During installation, finding the balance between the painting and the projection was hard: too bright and the projection cannot be seen, too dark and the painting cannot be seen. The projected text was also too small.
paragraphs.zh: 布展时，画与投影的平衡很难找：太亮投影看不到，太暗画看不到。投影的文字也太小。

caption.en: Room light reveals the painted surface while the projected image changes.
caption.zh: 环境光下的画布与不断变化的投影。

caption.en: The self-portrait used as input for the early prototype.
caption.zh: 早期原型用作识别输入的自画像。

caption.en: An early self-recognition interface. These experimental scores are not a measure of recognition accuracy.
caption.zh: 早期的自我识别界面。这里的实验分数并非识别准确率。

process_note.en: The lemon is the most direct annotation of structuralism: what we see is not the thing itself, but a product of all its relations with everything else. I rebuilt a 3D lemon from frames of Hollis Frampton’s Lemon (1969) with photogrammetry. These experiments are in the essay.
process_note.zh: 柠檬是对结构主义最直观的注解：我们看到的东西不是东西本身，而是它和其他所有东西之间所有关系的结合产物。我从 Hollis Frampton 的《柠檬》（1969）中提取画面、重建三维形体，这些实验都在论文里。
